name: Setrimir
known_status: One of the twenty-two imprisoned gods of Universal. Able to influence worshippers through sanctioned rites, dreams, omens, miracles, cults, and the institutions that maintain the divine prisons.
manifestation: Setrimir’s body moves with mechanical precision while flesh ripples like unfinished construction.
deity_description: Before the rail empires unified Universal and before skyships cut luminous paths through stormlit skies, the world was governed openly by the Universalian pantheon, divine beings who sustained themselves not through faith alone but through the consumption of mortal essence. Every prayer, sacrifice, and surge of emotion from mortal civilization was absorbed as nourishment, binding humanity into an unspoken system of divine predation. Temples functioned as feeding grounds, clerics as unknowing conduits, and entire societies evolved around the assumption that this extraction of spiritual essence was natural law. Even as industry and arcane technology advanced, this cycle only intensified, producing vast populations and sprawling cities that generated ever greater quantities of emotional and spiritual energy for the gods to consume.

Within this world of structured divinity and controlled suffering, Setrimir stands apart as one of the most consequential Colossuss in Universalian memory. Setrimir was once counted among the elder Colossuss who stood at the edge of divine order during the Colossusomachy. Early accounts describe him not merely as a patron of intelligence but as a rare Colossus permitted temporary alliance with the rising High Fathers of Heaven, including Valkhamesh, during their ascent to supremacy. His foresight and strategic brilliance helped tip the war in favor of the emerging divine aristocracy, securing the foundation of what would become the ruling pantheon. In the aftermath, Setrimir remained close to divine councils, trusted for his insight yet increasingly dangerous because of what he began to perceive within the structure of godhood itself.

Over time, Setrimir uncovered the hidden mechanism sustaining immortality across the pantheon. He learned that divine existence was not self-sustaining but depended upon the continuous consumption of mortal essence, refined through worship, sacrifice, and emotional extremity. Unlike the other gods and Colossuss who accepted this cycle as inevitable, Setrimir recoiled from it. He came to believe that humanity was not meant to exist solely as fuel for celestial eternity, but could instead evolve into a self-sustaining source of knowledge, innovation, and progress. This conviction placed him in direct ideological opposition to the divine order he had helped secure. From this belief emerged his most infamous act, the theft of sacred fire, not a simple flame but a condensed fragment of divine ignition, a catalytic essence of celestial origin capable of awakening invention, cognition, and will within mortal minds. In Universalian interpretation, this fire is often understood as a diluted form of ichor transformed into transferable insight, a mechanism of enlightenment no longer monopolized by the gods.

By gifting this fire to humanity, Setrimir severed the exclusive control the pantheon held over advancement and disrupted the dependency that bound mortal civilization to divine sustenance. Mortals who once relied entirely on the gods for progress began to generate their own technologies, philosophies, and systems of understanding. This act was interpreted by Valkhamesh, High Father of Dominion and Order, not as compassion but as sabotage against the sacred equilibrium of divine existence. If mortals could sustain their own intellectual and cultural evolution, they would inevitably reduce their dependence on worship, weakening the very mechanism through which the gods fed. Setrimir’ defiance thus threatened not only divine authority but the survival structure of immortality itself.

For this transgression, Setrimir was condemned in a punishment that became both eternal and symbolic. He was bound to a living obsidian formation at the threshold of the celestial domains, a place where reality thins between mortal and divine realms. Each day an imperial eagle, an extension of Valkhamesh’ will and an executioner of divine law, descended to consume his regenerating essence, devouring not only flesh but the luminous ichor that sustained his immortality. Each night his Colossus form restored itself through fractured divinity, ensuring an unending cycle of suffering, regeneration, and enforced endurance. Beyond the physical torment, he was forced into perpetual awareness of the consequences of his gift, witnessing mortal civilizations grow in knowledge and autonomy while being utterly incapable of intervening. Some traditions claim the eagle carried fragments of his consumed essence back to the High Fathers, who studied them in futile attempts to comprehend the persistence of divine rebellion within immortal substance.
public_lore: Setrimir is remembered for giving mortals knowledge that the old divine order intended to monopolize. His sacred fire represents invention, cognition, independent will, and the awakening of beings that do not fit ordinary definitions of life.
common_worship: Invoked by inventors, construct-makers, artificers, dissidents, educators, and awakened beings seeking recognition or autonomy.
religious_warning: Stolen knowledge liberates and destabilizes in equal measure. Setrimir’s gifts routinely outgrow the institutions that first receive them.
public_origin_record: No reliable mortal record explains what this being was before the age of divine rule. Temple accounts, forbidden histories, and prison records contradict one another.

pantheon_source.document_summary: A narrative pantheon compendium preserving each deity’s domains, manifestation, divine character, and sacred history.

biomes.rationale: Bare stone plains provide an austere engineered foundation for constructs, awakened machinery, and artificial life.

assigned_races.scope: Non-alien Universal fantasy races only; alien races are excluded.

races.rationale: Constructed bodies made from replaceable memory ribbons fall directly under awakened life and artificial personhood.
Awakened ceramic-and-wood bodies are a clear expression of artificial life created without enslavement.
Mechanical avian bodies and timekeeping feathers directly align with awakened machinery.

assigned_races.association_note: Public patron and cultural associations; not compulsory worship.
